description: Proofonauts is an online team combining AI engineering, software development, DevOps, cybersecurity, and UI/UX design. For Flame in Freefall, we plan to build FlareLedger: an interactive dashboard that summarizes, ranks, and explains NASA microgravity combustion research, with comparisons and links to original sources. We focus on reliable data, clear visualizations, and practical fire safety insights.
summary: FlareLedger helps students, researchers and engineers explore NASA microgravity combustion research without losing the evidence behind an explanation. Users browse investigations, inspect original records and units, trace sources, and compare compatible measured curves. Optional Gemini interpretations use selected public context, claim-bound citations and visible limitations. Our frozen snapshot includes ten NASA PSI investigations, nine experimental tables and six measured series with 1,844 original points. Built by the two-person Proofonauts team, the application combines source provenance with responsive browsing, persistent generation limits, monitoring and checked backups. It supports the Flame in Freefall challenge by making combustion evidence easier to explore and question. This is a research prototype, not validated fire-safety advice; full live answer evaluation and independent scientific review remain unfinished.
details:
FlareLedger is a source-linked research workspace for the challenge “Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data.” It helps students, researchers and engineers explore NASA combustion resources and inspect the evidence behind an interpretation.

Users browse investigations, search materials such as PMMA, inspect original table-row locators, open source records, explore FLEX measurements and compare compatible curves. Source identifiers, original units, file versions, DOI, missing values and limitations remain visible. The application distinguishes operating conditions from independent trials, droplet diameter from flame diameter, and historical incidents from measured experimental data. Matching units alone do not justify an overlay or a scientific conclusion.

Our frozen NASA PSI snapshot contains ten investigations, nine original tables and six measured series with 1,844 original points. Data come from BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, FLEX, SAME, SAME-R, SPICE and modeling/tomography metadata. PSI-62 contributes metadata rather than an included numerical simulation dataset. NASA historical and combustion guidance resources support contextual cards. We preserve source limitations instead of inventing missing measurements.

Ask adds an optional Gemini interpretation. Lexical retrieval selects bounded public source context; the model returns claims linked to context and source identifiers. The backend checks structure, exact context excerpts and citation markers. These mechanical checks do not prove scientific correctness or that every claim follows from its cited source. Retrieved evidence remains accessible when generation is unavailable. Persistent shared limits are ten reservations per rolling 24 hours, three per minute and one active call, without automatic retries or a paid fallback.

The application uses Vue 3, TypeScript and Vite, with Python 3.12, FastAPI and SQLite. Docker, GitHub Actions, HTTPS deployment, monitoring and checked off-host backups support delivery. The frontend runs on Vercel and the API on a VPS. Recorded checks for the PR22 baseline passed 163 backend tests; frontend checks passed 34 tests. Fifteen offline questions matched 45 source anchors. Those questions were used during development, not as a held-out benchmark. Full live answer evaluation and independent scientific review remain unfinished.

Proofonauts consists of exactly two people: Denys Voloshyn and Tymofii Chernoivanov. Denys coordinated scope, architecture, source preparation, SI integration and evaluation tooling. Tymofii coordinated infrastructure, deployment, monitoring, backups, reviews, interface checks, screenshots and branding. Together we practised source provenance, full-stack integration, bounded neural-network use, testing, Linux operations, Git review, backup recovery and English technical communication.

SI disclosure: ChatGPT/Codex assistance supported planning, code drafts, parsing and provenance tooling, tests, debugging, documentation, submission text, slide layout and speech preparation. Optional Gemini provides runtime interpretations; no model was trained or fine-tuned. Tymofii created the Proofonauts logo with neural-network assistance; the presentation visibly marks it as SI-generated. Original numerical measurements were not generated by a neural network. Product screenshots are real interface captures, and the slide showing a question form is not presented as a generated answer. The team reviewed changes and remains responsible for the result. No generated narration or video is included.

FlareLedger is an independent research prototype. NASA has not endorsed it, and it does not provide validated fire-safety advice. Next steps are independent answer review and broader source coverage.

Product: https://flareledger.fun/

Public code and documentation: https://github.com/Denofix/flareledger
